title: The Garden of the Glass Steppe
premise: Bram Joubert, a cartographer who once mapped the magical steppe-realm of Veyl before its covenant shattered and magic was outlawed, has hidden for three years as a charm-seller in the gray city of Corvane. When a dying courier presses a living map into her hands, she learns the barrier between realms is collapsing and only a descendant of the original cartographers can reforge it. Pursued by the city's anti-magic Wardens and shadowed by Sef, a Warden defector who once loved her, Bram gathers a found family of exiles and crosses the glass steppe to the ruined Covenant Spire. There she must choose between sealing the realms apart forever—keeping Corvane safe but dooming Veyl's dying people—or sacrificing her own memories of both worlds to bind them together. She chooses sacrifice, and wakes with no past but a garden growing where the steppe was glass, tended by the family that refuses to let her face the future alone.
about_author: Bram Montrose is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to fiction about places that refuse to be found. They live in a drafty house full of obsolete atlases and one opinionated cat.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In outlawed-magic Corvane, Bram sells harmless trinkets disguised as charms, keeping her true gift as a cartographer buried. A routine sale goes wrong when a Warden patrol nearly catches her. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a life built on hiding.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses in her shop, pressing a folded map into her hands and whispering 'the Spire remembers you' before dying. The map is alive, inked in Veyl-script only she can read. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant recognition—the past has found her.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Warden lieutenant Sef investigates the stranger's death and finds traces of real magic—and a familiar signature in the cartography. Ordered to hunt the map-bearer, he realizes it must be Bram. Emotional beat: duty grinding against old love.

chapters.title: The Map That Bleeds
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The living map shows the barrier between realms thinning; where it fails, glass spreads through Corvane's streets. Bram tries to destroy the map, but it reforms in her hands. Emotional beat: denial cracking—she cannot un-know what she knows.

chapters.title: Tally of the Broken
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Seeking answers, Bram visits Odji, a disgraced Veyli healer running an underground clinic. He confirms the covenant is failing and names her bloodline as the only key to the Covenant Spire. Emotional beat: the first fragile thread of found family.

chapters.title: Sef at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Sef corners Bram but hesitates when the map reacts to him too—he carries Warden-blood, a lineage bound to enforce the old covenant's ruin. He lets her go, lying to his superiors. Emotional beat: betrayal of duty begins as mercy.

chapters.title: The Night Market Beneath
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Odji leads Bram to Corvane's hidden night market to find a guide across the steppe. They recruit Pip, a feral young thief who can hear the glass singing. Emotional beat: wary strangers choosing to trust.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef's deception unravels; his commander orders the quarter burned to flush out the map-bearer. Sef warns the market at the cost of his rank and freedom. Emotional beat: the point of no return—he is now an exile too.

chapters.title: Out Through the Ash
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The fugitives flee burning Corvane through the aqueducts, Pip nearly dying to save the map. On the far side, the glass steppe stretches endless and blinding. Emotional beat: grief for the city that was never home, carried forward anyway.

chapters.title: Where the Glass Sings
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Crossing the steppe, Pip teaches the group to navigate by the glass's resonance; Bram realizes the steppe itself is the covenant, petrified. A storm of broken memory attacks them. Emotional beat: wonder braided with dread.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Sheltering in a frozen waystation, Bram confesses her history: her mother helped forge the covenant and was erased when it broke. The map has been leading Bram home to finish—or undo—her mother's work. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Sef, Unarmored
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef catches up to the group and surrenders his weapons rather than his purpose. Bram refuses to forgive him; Odji vouches for him anyway. Emotional beat: love against duty made flesh—trust extended before it is earned.

chapters.title: The Village Under the Veil
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The group reaches a hidden Veyli village, alive but fading as the barrier starves their realm. Its elder begs Bram to seal the rift permanently to save Corvane, accepting Veyl's death. Emotional beat: the moral weight of the choice ahead.

chapters.title: Pip's Bargain
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip, half-Veyli herself, learns sealing the rift means erasing everyone like her from existence. She runs into the glass fields alone and must be rescued from the singing storm. Emotional beat: found family tested by fear and fury.

chapters.title: The Third Path
chapters.summary: Odji's POV. Studying the map, Odji finds a third option in Bram's mother's marginalia: reforge the covenant not by sealing or breaking, but by binding it to a living cartographer's memory. The cost is everything Bram remembers. Emotional beat: hope arriving dressed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Warden's Hunt
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef's former commander, now wielding corrupted covenant-shards, pursues them to seize the Spire and rule both realms' ruins. A running battle on the glass costs Odji grave injury. Emotional beat: the enemy closes, and love makes them vulnerable.

chapters.title: Approach to the Spire
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The group reaches the Covenant Spire, a tower of fused memory-glass humming with Bram's mother's final work. Inside, the commander waits, offering Bram her old life back if she hands over the map. Emotional beat: temptation of the comfortable lie.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Climax. In the Spire's heart, Bram fights the commander while Pip and Sef hold the resonance-chambers. Choosing the third path, she pours her memories into the covenant as the Spire ignites. Emotional beat: self-annihilation chosen freely, as an act of love.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The barrier stabilizes; the commander is consumed by the shards she stole. Sef carries the memoryless Bram out of the collapsing Spire onto soil where glass used to be. Emotional beat: devastation and awe side by side.

chapters.title: The Garden Where Glass Was
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Weeks later, the steppe blooms into a garden-country open to both realms. Pip tends Bram, who knows no one's name but smiles at Sef's voice. Emotional beat: mourning someone still alive, and refusing to stop.

chapters.title: Names, Newly Given
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The found family tells Bram her own story piece by piece—Odji's clinics, Pip's thefts, Sef's long watch. Some memories return as dreams; others they simply retell until they feel true. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt by the people who love you.

chapters.title: The Map She Draws Next
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Standing at the garden's edge with a blank page, Bram feels the old gift stir—new realms are stirring beyond the reforged veil. She chooses to map forward, not back, with her family beside her. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope; the journey continues by choice.
